categories.main_business_segments: Qorvo operates through three main business segments: High Performance Analog (HPA), Connectivity and Sensors Group (CSG), and Advanced Cellular Group (ACG). HPA focuses on RF and power solutions for automotive, defense, aerospace, cellular infrastructure, and broadband. CSG provides connectivity and sensor solutions for IoT, smart home, automotive, and industrial markets. ACG delivers cellular RF solutions for smartphones, wearables, laptops, tablets, and other mobile devices.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Qorvo leverages a broad range of semiconductor process technologies, including gallium nitride (GaN), gallium arsenide (GaAs), silicon carbide (SiC), bulk acoustic wave (BAW), surface acoustic wave (SAW), silicon on insulator (SOI), silicon germanium (SiGe), and CMOS. The company operates internal wafer fabrication facilities in North Carolina, Oregon, and Texas, and assembly/test facilities in China, Costa Rica, Germany, and Texas, complemented by external foundry and assembly partners. Advanced packaging, module integration, and proprietary design methods are key to their manufacturing approach.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Qorvo's primary customers are leading U.S. and international OEMs and ODMs, with Apple and Samsung accounting for 37% and 12% of revenue, respectively, in 2023. The company serves markets including mobile devices (smartphones, wearables, laptops, tablets), cellular infrastructure, IoT and connected home, automotive, defense, and aerospace. End markets span consumer electronics, industrial, automotive, defense, and communications infrastructure.
categories.geographic_coverage: Qorvo operates globally, with significant presence in the Americas, Asia, and Europe. In fiscal 2023, 49% of revenue came from international shipments, with 43% from Asia (including 21% from China), and the remainder from the U.S. and other regions. The company maintains manufacturing, design, sales, and support facilities across North America, Asia, and Europe.
categories.supply_chain_position: Qorvo is primarily a midstream and downstream supplier, designing, manufacturing, and assembling advanced semiconductor components and modules that are integrated into end products by OEMs and ODMs. The company operates its own wafer fabs and assembly/test facilities, while also sourcing materials and some manufacturing services from external suppliers and foundries.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Qorvo's strategic focus is on innovation in RF, power, connectivity, and sensor technologies to address growing demand for high-performance, integrated solutions in mobile, IoT, automotive, and infrastructure markets. R&D priorities include advancing materials, process technologies (GaN, GaAs, BAW, SAW, SiC), packaging, and system integration. The company also pursues strategic acquisitions to complement its technology portfolio and expand into new markets.
categories.revenue_model: Qorvo generates revenue primarily through the sale of semiconductor products, modules, and solutions to OEMs, ODMs, and distributors. Revenue is recognized at the point of shipment or delivery, depending on customer terms. The company also provides foundry services and, to a lesser extent, licenses technology and IP.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Qorvo faces competition from major semiconductor companies such as Broadcom, Skyworks Solutions, Qualcomm, Analog Devices, Infineon, NXP, Texas Instruments, Wolfspeed, Murata, and others. The company is positioned as a leading supplier of RF, power, and connectivity solutions, with strong market share in mobile RF, defense, and select IoT and automotive segments. Many competitors have significant resources and established customer relationships.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2023, Qorvo reported revenue of $3.57 billion, down 23% from $4.65 billion in 2022, reflecting macroeconomic headwinds and lower demand for 5G handsets and other products. Operating income was $183 million, with a net income of $103 million. The company has over 8,500 employees and maintains a strong liquidity position, but recent growth has been challenged by market volatility and inventory corrections.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Qorvo differentiates itself through its broad and deep portfolio of high-performance, highly integrated RF, power, and connectivity solutions, leveraging advanced materials and proprietary technologies. The company emphasizes solving complex customer challenges, enabling smaller form factors, higher efficiency, and greater functionality, and supporting demanding applications in mobile, IoT, automotive, defense, and infrastructure markets.
